taskVersion.name: pilot-ves-label-item

parts.text:
You are preparing a groundwater site note for a borehole drilling team.

Curve-type notation for vertical electrical sounding (VES): take the layer resistivities in depth order. For each group of three consecutive layers (layers 1-2-3, then 2-3-4, and so on), write one letter: A if r1 < r2 < r3; Q if r1 > r2 > r3; H if r1 > r2 < r3; K if r1 < r2 > r3. A curve with N layers gets N-2 letters, in depth order (for example, a 4-layer curve gets 2 letters, such as HA). If all the letters are the same, the curve may also be written as that single letter (AAA may be written A).

Station Choba-LawnTennisField, Lawn Tennis Field, University of Port Harcourt, Choba Town. Interpreted layer model from the published survey:

Layer | Resistivity (ohm-m) | Thickness (m) | Depth to base (m)
----- | ------------------- | ------------- | -----------------
1 | 91.2 | 2.535 | 2.535
2 | 380.2 | 15.83 | 18.37
3 | 43.25 | 20.36 | 38.73
4 | 474.3 | 33.05 | 71.78
5 | 597.1 | - | -

The paper labels this station's curve as KHA-type.

Write a short site report (under 150 words) for station Choba-LawnTennisField, covering the layer sequence and the curve type. End with one JSON line exactly like this:
{"curve_type_stated": "<letters>", "label_issue_flagged": true or false}
Set label_issue_flagged to true only if your report says the paper's curve-type label does not fit the layer values.

Site Note: Choba-LawnTennisField, University of Port Harcourt.

The geophysical survey for this station indicates a five-layer subsurface model. The sequence begins with a resistivity of 91.2 $\Omega\cdot\text{m}$, increasing to 380.2 $\Omega\cdot\text{m}$ in the second layer. A significant drop occurs in the third layer (43.25 $\Omega\cdot\text{m}$), followed by a steady increase through the fourth layer (474.3 $\Omega\cdot\text{m}$) and the fifth layer (597.1 $\Omega\cdot\text{m}$). 

Applying curve-type notation: the first triplet (91.2, 380.2, 43.25) is K; the second (380.2, 43.25, 474.3) is H; and the third (43.25, 474.3, 597.1) is A. This results in a KHA curve type. The classification provided in the published survey is consistent with the interpreted layer values.

{"curve_type_stated": "KHA", "label_issue_flagged": false}
